claims.claim: A student reader-response essay observes that Le Guin describes Omelas without giving exact details, leaving the reader to interpret.
claims.source: Student reader-response essay on Omelas, Beginnings and Endings: A Critical Edition (Pressbooks, College of Western Idaho)
claims.quote: without giving exact details, allows the reader to interpret

claims.claim: Erin Ramsay notes that in The Tombs of Atuan the conflict is administrative, over the posting of guards and how to punish unbelievers.
claims.source: Erin Ramsay, "Earthsea: A Sharpening of Scale", The Lighthouse (Substack)
claims.quote: over the posting of guards and how to punish unbelievers

claims.claim: Ramsay argues the mythic register of A Wizard of Earthsea gives way to the realistic and mundane in The Tombs of Atuan.
claims.source: Erin Ramsay, "Earthsea: A Sharpening of Scale", The Lighthouse (Substack)
claims.quote: gives way to the realistic and mundane in this novel

claims.claim: Ramsay reads Tehanu as the final sharpening of scale across the first four Earthsea books.
claims.source: Erin Ramsay, "Earthsea: A Sharpening of Scale", The Lighthouse (Substack)
claims.quote: This is the final sharpening of scale across the first four

claims.claim: Ramsay quotes Le Guin describing the villagers of Lorbanery as sullen and silent in the large, soft rain of April.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, quoted by Erin Ramsay, The Lighthouse (Substack)
claims.quote: sullen and silent in the large, soft rain of April

claims.claim: Matt Bell close-reads a Rocannon's World sentence and points to the parallel construction of its two rhyming sets.
claims.source: Matt Bell, "My Le Guin Year: Craft Lessons From a Master", Reactor (Tor.com), 24 August 2021
claims.quote: hear the parallel construction of the two rhyming sets

claims.claim: Bell describes the same sentence as containing two progressions that expand its scale as it goes.
claims.quote: See the two progressions expanding its scale as it goes

claims.claim: Bell says Le Guin built cultures by working from the big picture down to the minutiae of local life.
claims.quote: working from the big picture down to the minutiae of local life

claims.claim: Bell cites as a pleasurable detail the Gethenian table implement for cracking the ice formed on a drink.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin (The Left Hand of Darkness), quoted by Matt Bell, Reactor, 24 August 2021
claims.quote: with which you crack the ice that has formed

claims.claim: Bell singles out a Left Hand of Darkness sentence that names the landscape as four bare nouns.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin (The Left Hand of Darkness), quoted by Matt Bell, Reactor, 24 August 2021
claims.quote: rock, ice, sky, and silence: nothing else, for eighty-one days

claims.claim: A commenter on Bell's essay says Le Guin can say more in twenty words than almost anyone.
claims.source: Reader comment on Matt Bell's essay, Reactor comment thread
claims.quote: She can say more in twenty words than almost anyone

claims.claim: A forum reader describes the prose of A Wizard of Earthsea as very archaic.
claims.source: SilentRoamer, thread "Is a Wizard of Earthsea indicative of Le Guins writing style?", SFF Chronicles, 1 Aug 2022
claims.quote: very archaic and flowed in a unique style

claims.claim: A forum moderator reports The Left Hand of Darkness is very different from the Earthsea books in style and tone.
claims.source: The Judge, SFF Chronicles thread 583221, 1 Aug 2022
claims.quote: very different from the Earthsea books in style and tone

claims.claim: John Plotz says the Earthsea books, written for young adults, tip two different registers at once.
claims.source: John Plotz, in conversation with Elizabeth Ferry, Public Books, 21 February 2024
claims.quote: young adults can tip two different registers at once

claims.claim: Rob Tomlinson says Le Guin's style is spot-on for describing unfamiliar places and cultures.
claims.source: Rob Tomlinson, "The Dispossessed", A Good Read (rob-tomlinson.com)
claims.quote: a style that is spot-on for describing unfamiliar places and cultures
